messages.content: I want an API that takes an IP address and returns company data with contact information if available.

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve data. This function is commonly used for API calls and web scraping. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The Date Nager API provides access holiday information for over 100 countries, including the ability to query for long weekends. It leverages ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes to tailor the search to your specific region of interest. More information can be found in https://date.nager.at/Api

headers.description: Optional headers to send with the request as a dictionary of header values.

Content-Type.description: The media type of the resource being requested, typically 'application/json'.

Authorization.description: The credentials to authenticate a user agent with a server, typically formatted as 'Bearer {token}'.

timeout.description: The maximum amount of time to wait for a response from the server, in seconds. A longer timeout may be necessary for slower network connections or overloaded servers. This is a float type value.

params.description: URL parameters to append to the URL. Sent as a dictionary of key-value pairs.

query.description: The query parameter for search or filtering.

page.description: The page number parameter for pagination. Used to retrieve a specific page of results.

auth.description: HTTP authentication credentials formatted as a (username, password) tuple.

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem), if required for the request.

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request as a dictionary of cookie names and values.

sessionid.description: Session identifier cookie, used to recognize client sessions on the server.

csrftoken.description: CSRF protection token cookie, used to prevent cross-site request forgery attacks.

proxies.description: Proxy settings as a dictionary, mapping protocol or protocol and hostname to the URL of the proxy.

http.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTP requests, including the port number.

https.description: Proxy URL to use for HTTPS requests, including the port number.

stream.description: Whether to stream the download of the response. If False, the response content will be immediately downloaded. Streaming is useful for handling large files or responses.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not. Set to False to skip certificate verification, which is not recommended unless you are sure of the server's identity.

message.content:
Below is a quick‑reference guide to the most popular public APIs that accept an IP address and return “company”‑level data (owner, organization, contact details, etc.). All of them expose a simple HTTP GET endpoint, usually require an API key, and return JSON. Pick the one that best matches your budget, data depth, and privacy requirements. | # | Service | Key Features | Typical Endpoint | Sample Request | Pricing (as of 2026‑06) | |---|---------|--------------|------------------|----------------|------------------------| | 1 | **ipinfo.io** | • Organization name, ASN, domain, company logo
• Contact email & phone (if available)
• Geo‑location, carrier, timezone | `https://ipinfo.io//json?token=` | `curl https://ipinfo.io/8.8.8.8/json?token=YOUR_TOKEN` | Free tier: 50k req/month. Paid: $5/mo for 1M req, $20/mo for 5M, etc. | | 2 | **ipstack.com** | • Company name, domain, industry
• Contact email, phone, website (paid tier)
• Geo‑location, ISP, ASN | `https://api.ipstack.com/?access_key=&fields=ip,hostname,company,contact` | `curl https://api.ipstack.com/8.8.8.8?access_key=YOUR_KEY&fields=ip,hostname,company,contact` | Free: 10k req/month. Paid: $10/mo for 100k, $50/mo for 500k, etc. | | 3 | **ipapi.co** | • Organization, domain, contact email (paid)
• Geo‑location, carrier, ASN | `https://ipapi.co//json/?key=` | `curl https://ipapi.co/8.8.8.8/json/?key=YOUR_KEY` | Free: 1k req/day. Paid: $9.99/mo for 100k, $49.99/mo for 500k. | | 4 | **ipgeolocation.io** | • Company name, domain, contact email, phone
• Geo‑location, ISP, ASN, timezone | `https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=&ip=` | `curl https://api.ipgeolocation.io/ipgeo?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&ip=8.8.8.8` | Free: 1k req/day. Paid: $9.99/mo for 100k, $49.99/mo for 500k. | | 5 | **ipwhois.io** | • Organization, domain, contact email (paid)
• Geo‑location, ASN, carrier | `https://ipwhois.app/json/?key=` | `curl https://ipwhois.app/json/8.8.8.8?key=YOUR_KEY` | Free: 1k req/day. Paid: $5/mo for 100k, $25/mo for 500k. | | 6 | **WHOISXMLAPI** (IP Address API) | • WHOIS data, company name, domain, contact email, phone, address
• Geo‑location, ASN, ISP | `https://www.whoisxmlapi.com/whoisserver/WhoisService?apiKey=&domainName=` (you first resolve IP → domain via reverse‑DNS) | `curl "https://www.whoisxmlapi.com/whoisserver/WhoisService?apiKey=YOUR_KEY&domainName=google.com"` | Free: 200 req/day. Paid: $19.99/mo for 1k, $99/mo for 5k. | | 7 | **IP2Location LITE** | • Company name, domain, contact email (paid)
• Geo‑location, ASN, ISP | `https://api.ip2location.com/v2/?key=&package_id=20&format=json&ip=` | `curl "https://api.ip2location.com/v2/?key=YOUR_KEY&package_id=20&format=json&ip=8.8.8.8"` | Free: 1k req/day. Paid: $9.99/mo for 100k, $49.99/mo for 500k. | --- ## How to pick the right one | Criterion | ipinfo.io | ipstack.com | ipapi.co | ipgeolocation.io | WHOISXMLAPI | |-----------|-----------|-------------|----------|------------------|-------------| | **Free tier** | 50k req/mo | 10k req/mo | 1k req/day | 1k req/day | 200 req/day | | **Contact info** | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | Yes (paid) | | **ASN / ISP** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | | **Geo‑location** | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | Yes | | **Rate limit** | 50k/mo | 10k/mo | 1k/day | 1k/day | 200/day | | **Ease of use** | Very simple | Very simple | Very simple | Very simple | Slightly more complex (needs reverse‑DNS first) | | **Pricing** | $5/mo+ | $10/mo+ | $9.99/mo+ | $9.99/mo+ | $19.99/mo+ | If you only need basic org/ASN data, **ipinfo.io** or **ipstack.com** are great starting points. If you need *contact* details (email, phone, address), you’ll have to upgrade to a paid tier on any of them, or use **WHOISXMLAPI** which pulls raw WHOIS records (often richer but less structured). --- ## Quick example (Python) ```python import requests IP = "8.8.8.8" TOKEN = "YOUR_IPINFO_TOKEN" url = f"https://ipinfo.io/{IP}/json?token={TOKEN}" resp = requests.get(url, timeout=5) data = resp.json() print("IP:", data.get("ip")) print("Hostname:", data.get("hostname")) print("Organization:", data.get("org")) print("Company:", data.get("company", {}).get("name")) print("Contact Email:", data.get("company", {}).get("email")) print("Contact Phone:", data.get("company", {}).get("phone")) ``` > **Tip:** Most services return a `company` object only on paid plans. On the free tier you’ll see `org` (e.g., `"AS15169 Google LLC"`) but no contact details. --- ## Final checklist before you start 1. **Define your data needs** – Do you need just the org name or full contact details? 2. **Check rate limits** – Estimate your monthly request volume. 3. **Verify compliance** – Some jurisdictions restrict sending personal contact info; ensure you’re compliant. 4. **Test the free tier** – Most services let you try the API with a limited quota. 5. **Secure your API key** – Store it in environment variables or a secrets manager. Happy coding! If you need help wiring up a specific provider or parsing the JSON, just let me know.
